rationale: Across postnatally evaluated clinical cohorts and reports of NDMSBA caused by biallelic PLAA pathogenic variants, global developmental delay/severe intellectual disability (HP:0001263 / HP:0001249) and progression from neonatal/infantile hypotonia to spasticity/spastic quadriparesis (HP:0001284 / HP:0002510) are consistently documented across affected individuals. For example, Falik Zaccai et al. (2017) observed global developmental delay and progressive spastic quadriparesis in all 7 of 7 patients (100%). Although prenatal cases (e.g., Huang et al., 2023) preclude functional neurodevelopmental scoring, all described postnatal cohorts confirm these two neurodevelopmental hallmarks as near-universal clinical features of the disorder.

evidence.text: Falik Zaccai et al. identified a novel form of leukoencephalopathy caused by homozygous PLAA loss-of-function variants, presenting in all seven evaluated patients between 2 and 4 months of age with progressive microcephaly, spastic quadriparesis, and global developmental delay.

new_directions.question_text: What specific biochemical markers in patient-derived fibroblasts or serum (e.g., cytosolic phospholipase A2 activity and prostaglandin E2 concentrations) best distinguish PLAA-deficient leukoencephalopathy from PEHO syndrome and classic atypical cerebral palsy?
new_directions.rationale: Because progressive microcephaly, spastic tetraparesis, and profound developmental arrest overlap extensively with other early-onset epileptic encephalopathies and white matter disorders, validating functional prostaglandin E2 and cPLA2 biomarkers could enable early biochemical discrimination before neuroimaging progression.

new_directions.question_text: Do hypomorphic missense variants outside the WD40 domain of PLAA permit survival past early childhood without progression to spastic tetraparesis?
new_directions.rationale: Dai et al. (2019) noted that mutations in the WD40 domain may carry a more severe clinical presentation, suggesting domain-dependent genotype-phenotype gradients that could alter long-term motor trajectory.
